questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Testing User Interactions”?
options: Testing User Interactions removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Testing User Interactions should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Testing User Interactions helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.

questions.answer_key: Testing User Interactions helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Testing User Interactions is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

Connect “Simulating input” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Testing User Interactions”?
options: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
